findings.summary: `_refetch_one` calls `orchestrator.analyze_and_store_item(item, source)` with no `learned_preferences` argument, so it defaults to `None`. Every other caller of this method sources it first: `run_once` calls `get_learned_preferences(self.storage)` (orchestrator.py:576) and threads it through `fetch_source_content` into `analyze_and_store_item` (orchestrator.py:491, :165), and the evaluator injects it straight into the LLM prompt when present (evaluator.py:135-139), materially affecting the priority assigned. Because refetch never sources it, every item recovered by `refetch` is evaluated and prioritized without the user's learned preferences from feedback -- a silent divergence from "the one analysis path" SC-1 established and that SC-2 says refetch reuses "in place". No test in the diff exercises learned_preferences for refetch, so this gap is unflagged.

The only assertion on SC-3's "real run ends with ... the summed real cost of the calls it made" is `assert report.real_cost is not None and report.real_cost >= 0.0`. The test drives real LLM calls through `local_pipeline_stub` (conftest.py:287-389), whose `/v1/chat/completions` response's `usage` object carries no `cost` field, and `llm_client.complete()` only requests OpenRouter's `usage.include` cost extension for an openrouter.ai host (llm_client.py:253-259) -- the local stub is neither, so `result.cost` is `None` for every call the test makes. `_real_cost_since` (refetch.py:311-340) therefore always sums to `0.0` in this test regardless of whether its run_id/event/status filtering is correct or entirely broken, and `>= 0.0` passes identically either way. The criterion's "summed real cost" claim is unproven by anything in the diff: this is the class of assertion that cannot fail.

`Storage.get_unreadable_content` is new and untested directly: no test in the diff seeds a mix of readable and not-readable items of the same source type to prove SC-2's "Readable items are never touched" clause is enforced by the selection query rather than by coincidence (every seeded row across every refetch test is already unreadable); none seeds more not-readable rows than `--limit` to prove the cap is respected; none seeds rows with distinct `fetched_at` values out of insertion order to prove "oldest first"; and none seeds an archived not-readable row to prove the `c.archived_at IS NULL` filter excludes it. All four are SC-2's own words ("stored, non-archived ... oldest first, bounded by --limit ... Readable items are never touched"), and a regression in any of the SQL's WHERE/ORDER BY clauses or the Python-side `is_readable` filter would pass every test currently in the diff.
